props.heading: Best trips from Denver on a budget
props.subheading: Real flight, hotel, and activity costs for the destinations that actually fit what you have to spend — flying out of DEN.

props.text: Aspen from Denver is barely a flight at all — 51 minutes in the air — and plenty of locals just drive instead. Flying out of DEN, a trip to Oaxaca can start around $1,164 for flight, hotel, and activities together — not just the flight, pulled from our own cost data, not guesses.

features.title: Las Vegas — nonstop, ~2h
features.text: Three airlines combine for about 114 weekly flights (roughly 16 a day) — one of Denver's highest-frequency leisure routes.

features.title: Oaxaca — no nonstop
features.text: Connects via Houston, Dallas, or Mexico City; total travel runs 4h44m–6h52m depending on the routing.

features.title: Aspen — nonstop, ~51 minutes (or a ~4-hour drive)
features.text: United flies it nonstop, about 52 flights a week — essentially a puddle-jump. Many Denver-area travelers drive the I-70/Hwy 82 route instead, since it lets them bring ski gear and skip the small-airport shuttle; expect up to 6 hours in bad snow or holiday traffic.

props.text: Las Vegas is a routine, high-frequency weekend run from Denver. Aspen is essentially in-state — the flight takes less time than getting to the airport for some people, which is exactly why so many Front Range travelers just drive the I-70 corridor instead and skip flying altogether. Oaxaca is the deliberate cultural trip of the three: no nonstop exists, so it's booked as a real vacation, not an add-on.

items.question: Are these real-time prices?
items.answer: They're estimates based on our own curated cost data for this route and season, not a live quote — the real price on the partner site may be a bit higher or lower depending on exact dates.

items.question: Should I fly or drive from Denver to Aspen?
items.answer: Flying takes just 51 minutes, but once you factor in security and the shuttle to/from Aspen's small airport, driving the roughly 4-hour I-70/Hwy 82 route is often comparable and more flexible — except on peak ski weekends, when traffic or avalanche-control closures can stretch it to 6 hours.

items.question: Is Oaxaca a quick trip from Denver?
items.answer: No — there's no nonstop, and connecting routes run 4h44m to 6h52m, so it's best treated as a dedicated trip rather than a quick escape.
